info.title: DomScan
info.description:
DomScan is a domain intelligence API providing domain analysis tools.

**Core Features:**
- Domain Availability: Check single or bulk domains using RDAP with 1,100+ TLDs supported
- Domain Intelligence: AI suggestions, valuations, health checks, typosquatting detection
- OSINT Tools: DNS lookup, WHOIS/RDAP, SSL certificates, subdomain discovery, IP geolocation, tech stack detection
- Social & Branding: Social handle checker, brand name scoring
- Phone Intelligence: Privacy-first phone number validation, normalization, and classification
- Pricing: Scheduled standard-TLD tables from verified official registrar sources, plus separate credential-backed exact-domain quotes
- Watchlist: Domain monitoring for expiration and availability alerts

**Authentication:**
Most API endpoints require authentication. Pass your API key via the x-api-key header or Authorization: Bearer header. Operations marked with an empty security requirement are intentionally public, including API specifications and selected catalog endpoints. Get your free API key at https://domscan.net/dashboard. Logged-in users on domscan.net tools pages are authenticated automatically via session cookie.

**Rate Limits:**
Free accounts can sustain 120 requests per minute per account, with a burst capacity of 60. All API keys and dashboard sessions belonging to the same free account share this budget.

Bulk endpoints have an additional free-tier budget of 20 HTTP requests per minute per account across all bulk endpoints. Free-tier bulk traffic is also capped at 100 requests per minute per IPv4 address or IPv6 /56 network. Platform-wide edge protections still apply to every tier.

Paid accounts can sustain 600 requests per minute, with a burst capacity of 120. API-key requests are counted per key; browser-session requests are counted per IP. Paid accounts do not receive the additional free-tier bulk budget.

Every authenticated response includes X-RateLimit-Plan, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Policy. X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining describe the immediate burst bucket; X-RateLimit-Policy also states the sustained per-minute rate, scope, and any free bulk limits. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After. Retry only after the indicated delay.

**Credits System:**
API calls consume credits based on endpoint complexity. Sign up for free to receive 10,000 credits monthly.
- 1 credit: Status checks, DNS lookups, tool builders
- 2-5 credits: Health checks, valuations, OSINT tools
- Bulk endpoints: standard per-item rate for batching multiple items into fewer HTTP requests.
- 6-25 credits: Recipe compound operations

When credits reach zero, the API returns HTTP 402 with credits_remaining, credits_required, and a purchase_url. API responses include X-Credits-Requested, X-Credits-Charged, and X-Credits-Refunded. Authenticated responses also include X-Credits-Remaining. Free credits refresh monthly on the account's signup anniversary.

**Error Handling:**
Standardized API errors return JSON with type, code, message, status, retryable, request_id, and docs_url. Temporary errors can also include retry_after. Some endpoints include additional fields such as suggestion, details, login_url, or credit details. Handle HTTP 200, 201, 400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 422, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 in your client. Common error codes: BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, NOT_FOUND, TIMEOUT, INTERNAL.

get.description: Return best-effort hostname evidence from public certificate and passive discovery sources. `sources=ct` is the only accepted compatibility selector. CT evidence uses the public append-only log model described by [RFC 9162](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html). DomScan does not brute-force labels or crawl the target site, so coverage is incomplete. Optional DNS verification checks only the names selected for the response and does not discover more. Wildcard evidence is returned separately when requested. Cache-only misses return 202 and all-source failures without stale cache return 503; both responses refund credits.

parameters.description: Compatibility selector. Only `ct` is accepted. It starts the passive discovery pipeline, but response entries identify the provider that supplied their evidence.

post.description: Retrieve one public HTTP(S) page with bounded redirects and response size. Standard uses one attempt, resilient permits one eligible retry, and rendered modes execute JavaScript in an isolated browser. Free accounts can use standard mode only, with 5 requests per minute, one concurrent request, 100 requests per day, 500 per month, and a 256 KiB response limit. Paid accounts allow 60 requests per minute, up to five concurrent standard or resilient requests, up to two concurrent rendered requests, and a 512 KiB response limit. CAPTCHA solving and premium proxy selection are not offered. Billing is based on processing effort, so target HTTP errors, blocks, rate limits, timeouts, and unsupported content remain charged. Invalid targets cost zero and verified DomScan platform failures are refunded.

Every accepted URL is charged at the selected mode price. Results are retained for 24 hours and job metadata for seven days. CAPTCHA solving and premium proxy selection are not offered. Target-site failures remain billed; items that cannot be processed because of a verified platform failure are refunded.

post.summary: Validate and normalize a phone number
post.description:
Validate one phone number against maintained international numbering-plan metadata and offline public-allocation data.

The endpoint accepts international numbers, national numbers with a two-letter default_country, extensions, Unicode digits, vanity numbers, short numbers with country context, and RFC 3966 tel: URIs. Parsing is strict, so unrelated text surrounding a number is rejected rather than silently extracted. Optional dialing_from_country adds caller-relative dialing formats, while language selects the language used for offline location and carrier labels.

The stable validation fields include E.164, international, national, and RFC 3966 formats, country or region, calling code, possible regions, number type, extension, country-match intelligence, and a decision-oriented status. The additive intelligence object can include a country-specific coverage level, numbering-plan location, possible time zones, original prefix carrier, regional portability support, dialing guidance, short-number signals, service classification, official allocation records, source provenance, and explicit accuracy warnings. United States results can match daily NANPA NPA-NXX central office code records. Canadian results can match nightly CNA/CNAC NPA-NXX status records. These sources describe prefix status and the original code holder, not the current carrier of a ported individual number.

**Privacy and scope:** The submitted number is checked using offline metadata and downloaded regulator snapshots. Customer lookups make zero paid or per-number third-party requests and the number is not persisted. A valid result means the number matches a current numbering-plan pattern. Location is a numbering-plan description, carrier is the original prefix carrier, and regulator data describes an allocated range. None proves that the individual number is assigned, active, reachable, owned by a particular subscriber, or currently served by any carrier.

**Credits:** 1 credit per number.
